questionText:
Let $G = (V, E)$ be an undirected unweighted connected graph. The diameter of $G$ is defined as:

$$\text{diam}(G) = \max_{u,v \in V} \{\text{the length of shortest path between } u \text{ and } v\}$$

Let $M$ be the adjacency matrix of $G$.
Define graph $G_2$ on the same set of vertices with adjacency matrix $N$, where

$$N_{ij} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } M_{ij} > 0 \text{ or } P_{ij} > 0, \text{ where } P = M^2 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$

Which one of the following statements is true?
explanation:
Step 1: Understand the edge additions in graph $G_2$
In graph $G$, $M_{ij} > 0$ means there is an edge (shortest path length 1) between vertex $i$ and vertex $j$.
The matrix $P = M^2$ gives the number of paths of length 2. Thus, $P_{ij} > 0$ indicates a path of length 2 exists between vertex $i$ and vertex $j$.

Step 2: Relate distances in $G$ and $G_2$
The adjacency matrix $N$ of $G_2$ sets $N_{ij} = 1$ whenever the shortest path distance in $G$, $d_G(i, j)$, is 1 or 2.
Thus, any path of distance $d$ in $G$ can be traversed in $G_2$ using at most $\lceil d / 2 \rceil$ edges.

Step 3: Compare diameters
Since the maximum shortest path distance in $G$ is $\text{diam}(G)$, the maximum shortest path distance in $G_2$ satisfies:
$\text{diam}(G_2) = \lceil \text{diam}(G)/2 \rceil$.

Hence, $\text{diam}(G_2) \le \lceil \text{diam}(G)/2 \rceil$ holds true.

Conclusion:
Option (A) is correct.
